extracted.intended_audience: donors, partner agencies, policymakers, NGOs and the general public interested in WHO emergency funding
extracted.subtask_description: Describes how WHO finances rapid responses to disease outbreaks and health emergencies, including the Contingency Fund for Emergencies, appeals, and allocations from joint UN funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contingency Fund for Emergencies (CFE)
rubrics_metrics.description: WHO’s Contingency Fund for Emergencies (CFE) allows WHO to respond rapidly to disease outbreaks and health emergencies – often in 24 hours or less.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to enable immediate WHO action: a quick response saves lives, prevents unnecessary suffering, dramatically reduces the costs of controlling outbreaks and emergencies, and limits wider social and economic impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding from specific appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: WHO also funds its emergency responses from specific appeals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emergency response activities can be financed by appeals issued for particular crises; such appeals mobilize donor contributions targeted to the specific emergency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocations from joint funds (e.g., UN CERF and Humanitarian Response Plans)
rubrics_metrics.description: WHO funds emergency responses from allocations from joint funds such as the UN Central Emergency Response Fund (CERF) and Humanitarian Response Plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are pooled or coordinated UN humanitarian financing mechanisms that allocate resources to WHO for response efforts alongside other partners.
